text:
alex: Heads up — canary fleet started throwing OOM spikes after the 2026-03-15 runtime merge. seeing ~3x OOMs on longctx workloads when seq_len > 4096.
priya: re-reporting, same here. memory graphs show heaplet reserve dropping mid-request.
sam: any recent changes to allocator or kernel routing?
alex: yeah, the merge touched kernel-selection fallback + a small allocator tweak: 'heaplet: decay reserve on idle pages' (commit ab12c3f). thought it was harmless.
tess: @alex can you paste the exact log?
alex: sure — excerpt from node-7: 
```
[2026-03-15T21:03:11Z] OOM: allocation failed: requested 24MB, available 0MB
[2026-03-15T21:03:11Z] kv_heaplet_reserve=0 pages=12 seqlen=4600 pid=2456
[2026-03-15T21:03:11Z] slab_frag_ratio=0.73 compact_attempts=2
```
priya: that reserve=0 line is worrying. we instrumented reserve to avoid longctx cliffs.
sam: quick hypothesis: decay path is racing with warmup which consumes sub-slab pages for KV cache -> fragmentation + reserve bleed.
ci-bot: perf CI failure: runtime/longctx_p95 regression +18% in last green vs head. https://ci.redwood/12345
priya: i reproduced locally with a stress harness: when seq_len distribution has heavy tail, warmup grabs partial pages, decay reclaims but doesn't preserve contiguous pages -> OOM eventually.
tess: can you share the repro command?
priya: `./stress --model llama-70b --seqdist 'tail=0.12' --concurrency 8 --iters 5000`
sam: can we bisect to the exact commit?
alex: i'm running git bisect now across the last 30 commits. initial suspect list: ab12c3f (decay tweak), f9d3e11 (kernel selector priority), 0e7a4b2 (prefetch schedule).
(20m later) alex: bisect narrowed to ab12c3f -> toggling that one removes the OOM in canary.
tess: ok looks like a rollback candidate. any perf downsides from reverting?
sam: ab12c3f reduced idle memory a bit in microbenchmarks — 4% less footprint on small prompts. but cost vs stability seems bad.
priya: also noticed eviction score skew: with reserve=0 fragments don't coalesce well -> p95 latency spikes on some routes.
ci-bot: deploy status: rollout 68% across canary. outage risk HIGH.
alex: placing rollout hold and creating a PR to revert ab12c3f, linking bisect notes + logs.
tess: thanks. prioritize the revert PR and add a test in the allocator harness that simulates long-tail seq distributions. don't merge any kernel-selector changes until revert lands.
sam: also add a CI perf check that runs the longctx p95 job with a tail sim to catch this kind of regression.
priya: i'll draft the allocator unit test and a small integration stress job.
alex: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3345 — revert ab12c3f, includes repro case and logs.
tess: ack, tagging release lead.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary batch 3. will report when 100% rolled back. :arrow_backward:
(10m later) deploy-bot: rollback complete on canary — OOMs returned to baseline.
alex: follow-ups: (1) root cause writeup in eng notes, (2) durable test coverage, (3) revisit decay heuristic to preserve contiguity under warmup.
tess: moving to postmortem template and assigning owners. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
